questions.question: Identify the dam that is located in South India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mettur dam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mettur Dam** stands as one of **India's largest and Tamil Nadu's** foremost, situated at the point where the **Kaveri River **enters the plains.
 
• Constructed in 1934, its completion spanned nine years. With dimensions reaching a maximum height of 214 feet and width of 171 feet, the dam collects water from its own catchment area as well as the Kabini Dam and Krishna Raja Sagara Dams in Karnataka.
 
• Adjacent to the dam lies Ellis Park, overseen by the Tamil Nadu Public Works Department.
 
• Serving over 12 districts in Tamil Nadu with irrigation and drinking water, the dam is hailed as the vital source of life and sustenance for the region. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rihand Dam** (Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar) is the second-largest dam in India by storage volume and is located in Sonbhadra district, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• **The Gandhi Sagar Dam **is among the quartet of major dams erected along India's Chambal River, situated in the Mandsaur district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• **Tilaiya Dam** marked the inaugural installment among the four multipurpose dams incorporated in the inaugural phase of the Damodar Valley Corporation. Positioned across the Barakar River, it stands at Tilaiya in the Koderma district of the Indian state of Jharkhand, inaugurated in 1953.

questions.question: What is the metric unit of pressure that is equal to 0.986923 atm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bar** is the metric unit of pressure that is equal to **0.986923 atm**.
 
• The bar is a unit of pressure equivalent to 100,000 pascals (100 kPa), though it is not formally recognized within the International System of Units (SI).
 
• At approximately 1.013 bar, it is slightly lower than the average atmospheric pressure experienced at sea level on Earth.
 
• According to the barometric formula, this pressure is akin to that found at an altitude of around 111 meters at a temperature of 15 °C.
 
• The concept of the bar, along with the millibar, was introduced by Vilhelm Bjerknes, a Norwegian meteorologist renowned for his contributions to modern weather forecasting practices. He defined the bar as one megadyne per square centimeter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **An atmosphere (atm) is a unit of measurement** representing the average air pressure at sea level, typically at a temperature of 15 degrees Celsius (59 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• One atmosphere is equivalent to 1,013 millibars or 760 millimeters (29.92 inches) of mercury.
 
• As altitude increases, atmospheric pressure decreases accordingly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The quart** is a volume measurement equal to one-fourth of a gallon. There are three types of quarts in use today: the liquid quart and dry quart within the US customary system, and the imperial quart within the British imperial system.
 
• **The gallon **is a unit of volume used in both British imperial units and United States customary units.
 
• **The yard **is a unit of length in both the British imperial and US customary systems, equivalent to 3 feet or 36 inches. Since 1959, it has been internationally standardized as precisely 0.9144 meters by agreement.

questions.question: Choose the INCORRECT statement related to monsoon.

options.text: The Southwest Monsoon winds blow over the warm oceans, gather moisture and bring widespread rainfall over the mainland of India.
The intensity and position of the high-pressure area, east of Madagascar, affects the Indian Monsoon.
The difference in pressure over Tahiti (Pacific Ocean), and Darwin in northern Australia (Indian Ocean) is computed to predict the intensity of the monsoons.
The western cyclonic disturbances occur due to withdrawal or the retreat of the monsoon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The western cyclonic disturbances occur due to withdrawal or the retreat of the monsoon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western cyclonic disturbances** are weather phenomena typically observed during the winter months.
 
• These disturbances manifest as low-pressure systems originating over the **Mediterranean Sea**. The term "Western" denotes the direction from which they approach India.
 
• These disturbances are characterized by cyclonic storms that develop over land, primarily in the Mediterranean region.
 
• They are often attributed to the temperature gradient resulting from the interaction between warm air from the tropics and cold air from the northern polar regions.
 
• This dynamic interplay of contrasting air masses gives rise to the formation of cyclonic disturbances, impacting weather patterns in regions along their path.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A monsoon** is traditionally characterized as a seasonal reversing wind accompanied by corresponding shifts in precipitation.
 
• However, its definition has evolved to encompass seasonal alterations in atmospheric circulation and rainfall patterns associated with the annual movement of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its northern and southern limits near the equator.
 
• Typically, the term "monsoon" denotes the wet phase of this seasonal pattern, although there is also a dry phase. Occasionally, it may refer to locally heavy yet short-lived rainfall events.
 
• The major monsoon systems worldwide include the West African, Asian–Australian, North American, and South American monsoons.
 
• These systems play significant roles in shaping regional climates and influencing precipitation patterns across vast geographical areas.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is a member of the actinide series?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thorium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thorium element **is a member of the **actinoid series**.
 
• Thorium, a chemical element denoted by the symbol Th and atomic number 90, is a weakly radioactive metal with a light silver hue. Upon exposure to air, it tarnishes to an olive-gray shade due to the formation of thorium dioxide.
 
• Characterized by its moderate softness and malleability, thorium boasts a high melting point. In terms of its chemical properties, thorium is classified as an electropositive actinide, with its chemistry primarily influenced by the +4 oxidation state.
 
• Notably reactive, finely divided thorium can ignite in air. All isotopes of thorium identified to date are unstable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The actinide or actinoid series** consists of at least 14 metallic chemical elements belonging to the 5f series.
 
• These elements have atomic numbers ranging from 89 to 102, covering actinium through nobelium. Although number 103, lawrencium, belongs to the 6d transition series, it is sometimes included in discussions of the actinide series.
 
• The name "actinide series" originates from the first element in the series, actinium. In general discussions of actinide chemistry, the informal chemical symbol "An" is often used to refer to any element within this series.
 
• According to the 1985 IUPAC Red Book, it is recommended to use "actinoid" instead of "actinide" because the suffix "-ide" typically denotes a negative ion. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnesium **is a mineral with an atomic number of 12 and an atomic mass of approximately 24.3 daltons (Da).
 
• **Lanthanum **is a silvery-white, soft, ductile, and malleable chemical element with the symbol La and atomic number 57.
 
• **Lutetium **is a silvery-white, solid chemical element with the symbol Lu and atomic number 71.

questions.question: In July 2018, an experiment aboard the International Space Station cooled a cloud of atoms of which chemical element to one ten-millionth of one Kelvin above absolute zero, forming a Bose-Einstein Condensate in space?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rubidium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2018, scientists at the **Cold Atom Lab **confirmed the production of **Bose–Einstein condensates (BECs)** from **rubidium atoms,** achieving temperatures as low as 100 nanoKelvin, just a fraction above absolute zero.
 
• This remarkable feat surpassed the typical temperature of space, which hovers around 3 Kelvin. However, the researchers aimed for even lower temperatures, aspiring to surpass previous Earth-based BEC experiments.
 
• Bose–Einstein condensates are a fascinating state of matter in condensed matter physics, emerging when a gas of bosons, a type of subatomic particle, is cooled to extremely low temperatures near absolute zero.
 
• At such chilly conditions, a significant portion of bosons occupy the lowest quantum state, revealing intriguing quantum mechanical phenomena at a macroscopic scale, such as wavefunction interference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In June 2020, the **Cold Atom Laboratory's experiment** aboard the International Space Station (ISS) marked a significant milestone.
 
• Successfully generating a BEC of rubidium atoms in microgravity, the experiment observed these atoms for over a second while in free-fall.
 
• This breakthrough, initially a proof of concept, yielded intriguing results, with approximately half of the atoms forming a magnetically insensitive halo-like cloud surrounding the main body of the BEC.

questions.question: In which type of tax is the marginal tax rate higher than the average tax rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Progressive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Progressive tax **is the** marginal tax rate higher than the average tax rate**.
 
• A progressive tax is characterized by a tax rate that rises as the taxable amount increases.
 
• The term "progressive" denotes the gradual increase in the tax rate, resulting in a taxpayer's average tax rate being lower than their marginal tax rate.
 
• This concept can apply to individual taxes or an entire tax system. Progressive taxes aim to alleviate the tax burden on individuals with lower ability to pay, shifting it more towards those with higher ability-to-pay.
 
• In contrast, a regressive tax, like a sales tax, imposes a larger proportion of the tax burden on the poor compared to the wealthy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A degressive tax** is one where individuals with higher incomes pay a smaller proportion of their income in taxes compared to those with lower incomes.
 
• **A proportional tax** is imposed with a fixed tax rate, meaning it remains constant regardless of changes in the taxable base amount. The tax amount is directly proportional to the taxable income.
 
• **A regressive tax** is one that extracts a larger percentage of income from low-income individuals than from high-income individuals.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts, enacted by the British Parliament, provided for the establishment of a Law Commission for the consolidation and codification of Indian Laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act, 1833**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Charter Act of 1833** marked a significant milestone in Indian legal history by **instituting a Law Commission** tasked **with the consolidation and codification of Indian laws.**
 
• Established in 1834, the inaugural Law Commission was helmed by TB Macaulay.
 
• Under Macaulay's leadership, the commission's recommendations paved the way for the formalization of the Criminal Procedure Code and the penal code, laying the groundwork for a more organized legal framework in India.
 
• Furthermore, the Charter Act of 1833 heralded a pivotal shift in India's administrative landscape by opening up avenues for Indian participation.
 
• It mandated that government employment be allocated based on merit rather than factors such as race, religion, color, or birth, signaling a move towards a more inclusive and equitable governance structure.
 
• Subsequently, the Charter Act of 1853 saw the establishment of the second Law Commission in England, commencing its operations in the same year. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indian Councils Act of 1909,** passed by the British Parliament, initiated some reforms in the legislative councils and partially expanded Indian involvement in the governance of British India.
 
• **The Government of India (GOI) Act of 1919 **marked a significant step by the administration towards the eventual introduction of responsible government in India, marking a pivotal moment in its governance.
 
• **The Charter Act of 1813,** also referred to as the East India Company Act of 1813, was legislation enacted by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the British East India Company for an additional 20 years.

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel ‘Before We Visit the Goddess’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Before We Visit the Goddess" **is a novel written by **Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni**.
 
• It explores the complex relationships between three generations of women in an Indian family spanning across India and the United States.
 
• The narrative weaves through themes of love, family, ambition, and the immigrant experience, offering a poignant exploration of the bonds that tie families together despite geographical and generational distances. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni **is an accomplished Indian-born American author, poet, and academic.
 
• Currently serving as the Betty and Gene McDavid Professor of Writing at the University of Houston Creative Writing Program, she has left an indelible mark on contemporary literature.
 
• Her collection of short stories titled "Arranged Marriage" earned her the prestigious American Book Award in 1996, showcasing her talent for capturing the complexities of human relationships within the context of Indian culture.
 
• Notably, her novels "The Mistress of Spices" and "Sister of My Heart," along with the short story "The Word Love," have been adapted into successful films, underscoring the widespread appeal of her storytelling. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Arundhati Roy**, born on November 24, 1961, is a prominent Indian author renowned for her groundbreaking novel "The God of Small Things" (1997). This masterpiece not only clinched the prestigious Booker Prize for Fiction in 1997 but also secured its place as the best-selling book by a non-expatriate Indian author.
 
• **Jhumpa Lahiri**, an English-born American novelist and short-story writer, intricately weaves tales that illuminate the immigrant experience, particularly that of East Indians.

questions.question: By which Indian Constitutional Amendment Act was the 11th fundamental duty added to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Constitutional Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Eighty-sixth Amendment to the Constitution of India** introduced the **Right to Education for children** aged six to fourteen years, along with Early Childhood Care up to the age of six.
 
• This amendment included the insertion of Article 21A, establishing the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right.
 
• Additionally, it replaced Article 45, which pertained to Early Childhood Education under the Directive Principles of State Policy. Furthermore, the amendment amended Article 51A, which outlines Fundamental Duties, to incorporate a new obligation for parents.
 
• The newly added duty mandates parents to ensure education for their children between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• This duty is enshrined as the 11th fundamental duty, emphasizing the importance of providing educational opportunities to children during this crucial period of development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Constitution (87th Amendment) Act, 2003,** brought about changes to the Constitution of India by replacing the 1950 national census as the basis for the delimitation of constituencies of the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
 
• **The Constitution (Eighty-eighth Amendment) Act, 2003, **introduced on March 7, 2003 and added service tax to the Union List and granted Parliament the authority to enact laws concerning taxes on specific services.
 
• **The 85th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2001** introduced the concept of "consequential seniority" in the promotion of government servants belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.question: The natural vegetation of India is broadly divided into _______ groups.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** boasts a rich and diverse array of natural vegetation, owing to its varied climatic conditions and geographical features.
 
• This natural vegetation can be broadly categorized into **five main types**:
 
• **Tropical Evergreen Forest: **These dense forests are characterized by lush greenery and high rainfall throughout the year. They are found in regions with warm and humid climates, such as the Western Ghats, northeastern states, and parts of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forest:** Also known as monsoon forests, these forests experience distinct wet and dry seasons. They shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve water. Tropical deciduous forests are widespread in central and eastern India, including parts of the Deccan Plateau and the Eastern Ghats.
 
• **Thorny Bushes in Deserts:** Found in arid and semi-arid regions, such as the Thar Desert in Rajasthan, these vegetation types are adapted to survive in harsh desert conditions. They consist of drought-resistant plants like cacti and thorny shrubs.
 
• **Mountain Vegetation:** As altitude increases, vegetation varies based on temperature and precipitation. Mountain vegetation includes alpine meadows, coniferous forests, and temperate broadleaf forests. These vegetation types are found in the Himalayan region, including states like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• **Mangrove Forest:** Mangroves thrive in coastal areas with brackish water and are characterized by salt-tolerant trees and shrubs. They provide important habitats for various marine species and act as natural barriers against coastal erosion. Mangrove forests are found along the coastlines of states like West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's natural vegetation is shaped by factors such as **soil composition, climate, topography, and precipitation **patterns.
 
• This diverse range of flora and fauna contributes to India's rich biodiversity and ecological significance.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders founded the women’s wing of Congress in 1940?

The correct answer is __**Sucheta Kriplani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sucheta Kriplani was **among the freedom fighters who founded the **women's wing of Congress** in 1940.
 
• Sucheta Kripalani was India's inaugural female Chief Minister, leading the Uttar Pradesh government from 1963 to 1967.
 
• Like her contemporaries Aruna Asaf Ali and Usha Mehta, she rose during the Quit India Movement and faced arrest by the British.
 
• She later collaborated closely with Mahatma Gandhi during the Partition riots, accompanying him to Noakhali in 1946.

• Currently, Alka Lamba holds the position of president of the All India Mahila Congress, assuming office on January 5, 2024.
 
• The AIMC operates through regional branches known as Pradesh Mahila Congress (State Women's Congress), which represent the AIMC in various states and union territories of India.
 
• These Pradesh Mahila Congress units are responsible for overseeing the affairs of AIMC within their respective regions. Membership in AIMC is comprised of women who are card-carrying members of the Indian National Congress. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lakshmi Sahgal **was a key figure in the Indian independence movement, serving as an officer in the Indian National Army and later as the Minister of Women's Affairs in the Azad Hind government.
 
• **Sarojini Naidu,** renowned as both a political activist and poet, made history as the first Governor of the United Provinces following India's independence.
 
• **Aruna Asaf Ali**, an educator, political activist, and publisher, played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement. She is best remembered for her courageous act of hoisting the Indian National flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan in Bombay during the Quit India Movement of 1942.

questions.question: 'The Great Indian Novel’ is written by _____ in which he based ‘The Mahabharata’ as a framework for his satirical novel.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shashi Tharoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"The Great Indian Novel" **by **Shashi Tharoor,** published in 1989 by **Viking Press,** is a satirical masterpiece. This fictional work cleverly reimagines the epic Mahabharata within the backdrop of the Indian Independence Movement and the ensuing years.
 
• Tharoor's narrative is rich with puns and references to renowned literary works on India, including those by Rudyard Kipling, Paul Scott, and E. M. Forster.
 
• Structured akin to the Mahabharata, the novel is divided into sections and chapters that mirror the organization of the epic.
 
• Each segment skillfully alludes to themes and events from its counterpart in the Mahabharata, lending depth and complexity to the narrative.
 
• With 18 "books" akin to the 18 books of the Mahabharata and the 18-day Battle of Kurukshetra, Tharoor masterfully weaves together history, mythology, and satire in this remarkable work. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• It achieves this by irreversibly deactivating the cyclooxygenase (COX) enzyme.
 
• Aspirin, along with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), is highly effective in alleviating skeletal pain, including discomfort associated with conditions like arthritis.
 
• Moreover, aspirin acts as a non-addictive analgesic, meaning it relieves pain without causing dependence.
 
• By impeding the production of prostaglandins, aspirin helps mitigate inflammation in tissues, thereby reducing pain sensations.

• **Pyrite**, commonly referred to as fool's gold, is a mineral composed of iron and sulfur.

• **The Siddheshvara Mahadeva temple**, located in Barakar, Burdwan District, West Bengal, stands as an exemplary representation of the early **Pala style of architecture.**
 
• This distinctive style, prevalent from the 9th to the 11th centuries in Bengal and Bihar, derives its name from the Pala dynasty that reigned over the region during that era.
 
• Constructed in the 9th century, the Siddheshvara Mahadeva temple is a Hindu religious edifice characterized by its unique architectural features.

• Gopala's successor, Dharmapala, reigned from around 770 to 810 and significantly expanded the kingdom, even briefly controlling Kannauj.
 
• Under the reign of Devapala (approximately 810–850), Pala dominance was sustained through military campaigns that extended into northern regions, the Deccan, and the peninsula.
 
• However, subsequent to Devapala's era, the dynasty witnessed a decline in power. Mahendrapala, the Gurjara-Pratihara emperor of Kannauj during the late 9th and early 10th centuries, even managed to penetrate northern Bengal.

• **The Hussain Shahi dynasty,** a familial lineage, assumed authority over the late medieval Sunni Muslim Sultanate of Bengal, reigning from 1494 to 1538.

questions.question: Which Goddess is associated with the Gangaur Festival celebrated in Central and Western India?

• It is dedicated to the worship of Goddess Gauri (Parvati), the consort of Lord Shiva, and is observed with great zeal and devotion during the Hindu month of Chaitra, which typically falls in March or April.
 
• The festival symbolizes various aspects including the arrival of spring, the harvest season, marital fidelity, conjugal happiness, and fertility.
 
• Women play a central role in the celebrations, offering prayers to Goddess Gauri for blessings related to marriage, marital bliss, and the well-being of their husbands. Unmarried women seek the blessings of the goddess for a suitable life partner, while married women pray for the health, longevity, and prosperity of their husbands.
 
• Gangaur is characterized by colorful processions, traditional rituals, and cultural performances that showcase the rich heritage and traditions of the region. It serves as a time for communities to come together, celebrate, and express gratitude for the blessings bestowed upon them.

• **Kali **is a significant Hindu goddess associated with various aspects including time, change, creation, power, destruction, and death in the Shaktism tradition. She is often depicted as fierce and fearsome, representing the raw power of nature and the cycle of life and death.

The correct answer is __**5.1 feet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The height of a badminton net **is set at **1.55 meters (5 feet 1 inch)** at the edges and 1.524 meters (5 feet) high in the center.
 
• This variation in height ensures proper clearance for the shuttlecock during gameplay, with the net being slightly higher at the sides compared to the center.
 
• Badminton nets span the entire width of the court, which is 20 feet (6.1 meters), and are positioned over the doubles sidelines, regardless of whether singles or doubles matches are being played.
 
• A standard badminton court, marked out for both singles and doubles matches, measures 13.41 meters (44.00 feet) in length and 6.10 meters (20.00 feet) in width. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Badminton** is a racquet sport where players use racquets to hit a shuttlecock across a net. While it can be played with larger teams, the most common formats are "singles" (one player per side) and "doubles" (two players per side).
 
• Badminton is often enjoyed as a casual outdoor activity in yards or on beaches, while formal matches take place on rectangular indoor courts.
 
• The shuttlecock, typically made of feathers or, in informal settings, plastic, has a distinct flight pattern different from the balls used in many other sports. Badminton evolved from the earlier game of battledore and shuttlecock, originating in British India.
 
• European play historically saw domination from Denmark, but the sport has gained immense popularity in Asia, particularly with China's recent dominance in competitions.
 
• Badminton made its debut as a Summer Olympic sport in 1992, initially featuring four events: men's singles, women's singles, men's doubles, and women's doubles. Mixed doubles was later added to the Olympic program four years later.

questions.question: When the President of India keeps a bill (except money bill and constitutional amendment bill) pending for an indefinite period, it is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pocket veto of the President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A pocket veto** is the term used when the **Indian president **delays a law indefinitely. 
 
• A pocket veto is a type of legislative technique that permits the president to veto a bill without actually acting on it. This basically vetoes the law without giving it a positive vote. 
 
• The bill is neither rejected by the president nor sent back for more examination. The President is not subject to a time constraint under the Constitution to act on the bill. 
 
• Gyani Zail Singh was the first president to exercise a pocket veto.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• When a president receives a measure and is unable to reject it and send it back to Congress within ten days, this is known as a pocket veto.
 
• Despite the absence of official objections and a signature, the bill does not become law.
 
• The veto override procedure in Congress does not apply to pocket vetoes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A simple majority can override a suspensive veto, sometimes referred to as a suspensory veto.
 
• The ability to refuse to provide the president of India's consent to a measure that has been passed by parliament is known as the absolute veto.
 
• The president can offer suggestions for improving a measure through an amendatory veto. Within ten days of the bill's passing, the president is required to veto it.

questions.question: Who among the following is considered the ‘Father of Carnatic Music in India’?
questions.solution:

• From modern-day Karnataka, India, Srinivasa Nayaka, also called Purandara Dasa, was a composer, vocalist, and Haridasa philosopher.
 
• He adhered to Madhvacharya's Dvaita school of thought. He was a leading pioneer in the field of Carnatic music.
 
• He is known as the Pitamaha (literally, "grandsire") of Carnatic music because of his enormous contributions to the genre.
 
• He is regarded as an incarnation of Narada, so goes the mythology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• According to the languages of the** South Indian subcontinent**, the music system known as Carnatic music is typically connected to South India, which includes the present-day Indian states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Telangana.
 
• It is one of two primary Indian classical music subgenres that originated with ancient Hindu writings and customs, especially the Samaveda. Hindustani music is the other subgenre; it became unique due to Persian or Islamic influences from Northern India.
 
• Carnatic music primarily emphasizes vocal music; most pieces are supposed to be sung, even when played on instruments; one should execute them in a gāyaki (singing) style.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a capital expense?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Construction of school buildings**__.

__
 
• **The construction of school buildings** is considered a** capital expense**.
 
• **Capital expenses** are those expenditures incurred to acquire, upgrade, or improve long-term assets, such as buildings, equipment, or land, that are expected to provide benefits over multiple accounting periods.
 
• In the context of school buildings, constructing or renovating a facility typically involves significant expenditure and is intended to provide a long-term benefit by providing a space for education and learning over many years.
 
• Therefore, the costs associated with constructing school buildings are classified as capital expenses rather than operating expenses, which are typically incurred for day-to-day operations and maintenance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pension** benefits are indeed typically classified as a non-operating expense.
 
• **Salaries expense, **payable to employees, is typically categorized as an operating expense. However, its classification as either an administrative expense or a selling expense depends on the function of the employee.
 
• **Subsidies **are considered revenue expenditures since they neither generate assets nor decrease government liabilities.

questions.question: Terrestrial planets are composed of ______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rocks and metals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Terrestrial planets, **resembling Earth in composition, consist mainly of** rocks or metals and possess solid surfaces**.
 
• They typically feature a dense, molten core composed of heavy metals, and exhibit distinctive topographical characteristics such as valleys, volcanoes, and craters. These planets also tend to have a limited number of moons.
 
• In our solar system, the four terrestrial planets—**Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars**—are the closest to the sun. During the solar system's formation, it is believed that there were more terrestrial planetoids, but many either merged with each other or were fragmented and destroyed.
 
• Mercury, the smallest of the terrestrial planets, is roughly one-third the size of Earth.
 
• It has a thin atmosphere, causing extreme temperature fluctuations, swinging between scorching heat and freezing cold.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Among the four terrestrial planets, Earth stands out as the largest and the only one boasting extensive regions of liquid water, a vital ingredient for supporting life as we know it.
 
• Earth is teeming with life, from the depths of its oceans to the peaks of its mountains.
 
• Like its terrestrial counterparts, Earth features a rocky surface adorned with mountains and canyons, and harbors a dense, heavy-metal core beneath its crust. Moreover, Earth's atmosphere contains water vapor, contributing to the planet's ability to regulate and moderate daily temperatures. 
 
• This unique combination of factors makes Earth a remarkably hospitable and diverse environment, fostering the flourishing of a wide array of life forms.

questions.question: Losar (a new year festival) is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Losar **is a vibrant new year festival observed in **Arunachal Pradesh and Ladakh**, deeply rooted in Buddhist traditions.
 
• Occurring on the first day of the Tibetan lunar calendar, Losar heralds the arrival of spring and symbolizes the onset of new beginnings.
 
• Central to the festivities are rituals aimed at dispelling malevolent forces and invoking auspicious energies. Across regions like Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh, Losar unfolds over a 15-day period marked by fervent celebrations.
 
• Communities come together to adorn their homes, engage in religious observances, and prepare elaborate offerings for divine entities. In the spirit of hospitality, people welcome both kinfolk and strangers alike.
 
• Amidst the jubilant atmosphere, traditional delicacies like "kapse," a special type of cake, and "chang," a fermented alcoholic beverage, are savored with gusto, adding to the festive cheer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**, often referred to as the 'Dawn-Lit Mountain Province,' is a state nestled in the northeastern region of India. 
 
• Established on February 20, 1987, it emerged from the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) territory. The capital and largest town of Arunachal Pradesh is Itanagar. 
 
• This state shares its borders with the Indian states of Assam and Nagaland to the south, while its international boundaries extend to Bhutan in the west and Myanmar in the east. 
 
• Notably, Arunachal Pradesh also shares a disputed border of 1,129 km with China's Tibet Autonomous Region to the north, demarcated by the McMahon Line. 
 
• Although China claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of the Tibet Autonomous Region, its occupation of certain regions in 1962 was subsequently reversed.

questions.question: In which year did the 44th Amendment remove the right to property from the list of fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1978**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 44th Amendment to the Constitution**, enacted in 1978, brought significant changes to India's legal framework. Notably, it removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights and reclassified it as a simple legal right under Article 300 A.
 
• This amendment was introduced as a response to the amendments made under the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, which had altered several provisions of the Constitution.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act aimed to reverse these changes and protect the rights of citizens against potential future infringements by the majority.
 
• It's important to note that the 44th Amendment Act was introduced as a bill under the 45th Amendment Bill in 1978.
 
• Its enactment was seen as crucial in safeguarding the interests of the nation and ensuring the preservation of fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 44th Amendment Act of 1978** was a significant step in restoring balance to India's constitutional framework.
 
• It reversed a provision introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act, which had granted the government extensive power to amend the Constitution at will under Article 368.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act effectively nullified this unchecked authority, ensuring that future constitutional amendments would be subject to proper scrutiny and safeguards.
 
• Additionally, the 44th Amendment Act reclassified the Right to Property, previously enshrined as a Fundamental Right under Article 31, as a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• This change reflected a shift in the constitutional perspective on property rights, aligning them more closely with other legal rights while still affording protection to property owners.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 77**__.

__
 
• **Article 77 of the Constitution of India **pertains to the Conduct of business of the Government of India and outlines several provisions:

 
 
• All executive actions of the Government of India must be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.
 
• Orders and other instruments made and executed in the name of the President must be authenticated in a manner specified by rules established by the President.
 
• The validity of such orders or instruments, when properly authenticated, cannot be challenged on the grounds of not being made or executed by the President.
 
• The President is authorized to create rules for the more convenient transaction of the Government of India's business and for the distribution of this business among Ministers.

• **Article 67** of the Constitution states the procedure for the removal of the Vice President. According to this article, the Vice President can be removed from office by a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha with an effective majority (i.e., a majority of the total membership of the House), and agreed to by the Lok Sabha with a simple majority (i.e., a majority of the members present and voting).
 
• **Article 48** of the Constitution of India is one of the Directive Principles of State Policy. It directs the state to endeavor to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle, thereby promoting their protection and welfare.

questions.question: Identify the third germinal layer found in triploblastic animals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mesoderm__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The third germinal** layer found in triploblastic animals is the **mesoderm**.
 
• The mesoderm, positioned between the ectoderm and endoderm, is the middle layer among the three germ layers formed during gastrulation in early embryo development across most animals.
 
• It gives rise to various structures such as mesenchyme, mesothelium, non-epithelial blood cells, and coelomocytes.
 
• Mesothelium lines coeloms, while mesoderm contributes to the formation of muscles through myogenesis, as well as septa and mesenteries.
 
• Additionally, it plays a role in forming parts of the gonads, with myogenesis specifically driven by mesenchyme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The ectoderm,** positioned as the outermost layer among the three primary germ layers, develops during early embryonic development. It lies superficially to the mesoderm (the middle layer) and the endoderm (the innermost layer).
 
• **A coelom** serves as a fluid-filled cavity that shields the internal organs of numerous organisms, functioning as the body cavity in animals.
 
• **Endoderm, **constituting the innermost layer of the embryo, contributes to the formation of the digestive tract and various other bodily structures.

• The money bill's certificate is approved by the Speaker of the House of People. It says that it's a money bill and is signed by him/her.
 
• When it is submitted to the President for ratification under article 111 and sent to the Council of States under article 109, it is considered endorsed.
 
• Article 110 of the Indian Constitution defines money bill. Money bills deal with money-related issues such as taxes and public spending. 
 
• The lower chamber of the Indian Parliament is called the Lok Sabha, and its speaker is its highest authority and presiding official.
 
• In the Lok Sabha's first meeting after the general elections, the speaker is chosen by the whole assembly. The speaker, who holds a five-year term, is selected among the Lok Sabha's current members.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts prevents disrespect to the National Flag and National Anthem?

options.text: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act of 1971** serves to safeguard the integrity of the **National Flag, National Anthem, and Constitution of India. **This legislation imposes penalties on individuals who display disrespect towards these national symbols.
 
• Offenders can face imprisonment for up to three years, a monetary fine, or both. The Act also regulates the proper hoisting, usage, and exhibition of the Indian National Flag.
 
• Among its provisions are prohibitions against allowing the flag to touch the ground or be draped over vehicles, buildings, or other objects. Additionally, intentional display of the flag with the saffron color facing downwards is deemed inappropriate.
 
• The Supreme Court has clarified that respectful standing during the National Anthem, even if not sung, does not constitute a violation of the Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Part IVA of the Indian Constitution** outlines the fundamental duties of Indian citizens, which include adhering to the Constitution, respecting its principles and institutions, as well as honoring the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• The corresponding Act elaborates on the penalties for contravening Article 51Aa of the Constitution.
 
• According to this Act, individuals holding high-ranking positions such as the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and other government officials can face disqualification if found guilty of violating the Constitution, as per sections 7 and 8(k) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
• In instances where the judiciary annuls unconstitutional actions of the executive, these actions are deemed as written acts visible to the public, thereby constituting contempt of the Constitution of India or its provisions.

questions.question: Which of the following Governor Generals, under the British rule in India, professionalised, bureaucratised and Europeanised the administration of East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Cornwallis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Cornwallis,** who served as** Governor-General of India from 1786 to 1793,** is credited with professionalizing, bureaucratising, and Europeanising the administration of the East India Company during his tenure.
 
• He implemented significant administrative reforms, including the establishment of the civil services and the introduction of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, which aimed to create a more stable revenue system. 
 
• Lord Cornwallis introduced several administrative reforms during his tenure, including the codification of laws, the establishment of district-level courts, and the separation of executive and judicial functions.
 
• These measures aimed to streamline the administration and enhance the Company's control over its territories in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Charles Canning, **also known as the Viscount Canning and Clemency Canning, was a British statesman who served as Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and became the first Viceroy of India after the transfer of power from the East India Company to the Crown of Queen Victoria in 1858.
 
• **Warren Hastings** FRS was a British colonial administrator, serving as the first Governor of the Presidency of Fort William, the head of the Supreme Council of Bengal, and consequently the first Governor-General of Bengal from 1772 to 1785.
 
• **James Andrew Broun-Ramsay**, 1st Marquess of Dalhousie KT PC, known as the Earl of Dalhousie between 1838 and 1849, was a Scottish statesman and colonial administrator in British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The East India Company (EIC)** was an English, and later British, joint-stock company founded in 1600 and dissolved in 1874.
 
• It was established for trade in the Indian Ocean region, initially with the East Indies (the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia), later expanding to East Asia.
 
• The company gained control of significant parts of the Indian subcontinent and established colonies in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong.
 
• At its zenith, it was the world's largest corporation by various measures and maintained its own armed forces with the company's three presidency armies, totaling about 260,000 soldiers, twice the size of the British army at the time.

questions.question: Who was the first ecologist to describe the specific shape of eco-trophic interactions,Which he called the pyramid of numbers, in the 1920s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charles Elton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charles Elton** was the **first ecologist** to describe the specific shape of eco-trophic interactions, Which he called the pyramid of numbers, in the 1920s.
 
• He was an esteemed English zoologist and animal ecologist, is credited with pioneering the concept of the ecological pyramid in 1927.
 
• Elton also introduced the term "pyramid of numbers" to elucidate the phenomenon where lower trophic levels typically harbor a greater number of individuals compared to higher trophic levels.
 
• Ecological pyramids serve as graphical representations delineating the interrelationships among different organisms across various trophic levels.
 
• These pyramids elucidate the relative quantities of diverse parameters across trophic levels, encompassing factors such as the abundance of organisms, energy flow, and biomass distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ernst Haeckel,** a renowned German zoologist and evolutionist, staunchly advocated for Darwinism and put forth innovative concepts regarding the evolutionary ancestry of humans.
 
• **Howard Thomas Odum,** commonly referred to as H. T. Odum, was an influential American ecologist celebrated for his groundbreaking contributions to ecosystem ecology. He also proposed thought-provoking extensions to the laws of thermodynamics, drawing from his insights into general systems theory.
 
• **E.O. Wilson**, an esteemed American biologist, is widely acclaimed as the foremost expert on ants globally. His extensive research and expertise have significantly advanced our understanding of ant behavior and ecology.

questions.question: Famous musician Talvin Singh is associated with playing the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tabla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Talvin Singh **is an English musician, producer, and composer known for his expertise in playing the tabla.
 
• He gained recognition for pioneering a unique fusion of Indian classical music with drum and bass, contributing to the emergence of the electronica subgenre known as Asian Underground.
 
• Singh's collaborations with artists like Siouxsie and the Banshees and Björk in the early 1990s propelled him into the spotlight.
 
• His debut album, "Ok," released in 1999, earned him the prestigious Mercury Music Prize.
 
• In 2010, Singh received an award at the UK Asian Music Awards for his "Commitment to Scene." In recognition of his contributions to music, he was honored with an OBE in the 2014 Birthday Honours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A tabla** is a pair of hand drums originating from the Indian subcontinent. Since the 18th century, it has held a central role as the principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is versatile, being played solo, accompanying other instruments and vocals, and as part of larger ensembles.
 
• The tabla is prevalent in popular and folk music performances across India, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.
 
• It holds significance in the devotional practices of Hinduism and Sikhism, often used during bhajan and kirtan singing.
 
• Sufi musicians commonly use the tabla in qawwali performances, and it is a prominent feature in dance forms like Kathak. As a rhythmic instrument, the tabla plays a crucial role in various musical traditions.
